title: security-eng-sync-notes-2026-03-04
content:
Security Engineering Sync - Notes
Date: 2026-03-04
Facilitator: Samira Patel
Attendees: Samira, Jon, Priya, Liam, Maya (+ async updates from Carlos)

Agenda:
- Weekly vuln triage
- Secrets scanning false positives + rollout plan
- Threat modeling backlog prioritization
- Action items & owners

1) Vulnerability triage
- Summary: Went through last week's scanner output (Snyk + internal fuzzing). Primary noisy items: a transitive dependency in ml-runtime (SEC-412), CVE-2026-1023 flagged in monitoring-agent (low severity, but widespread), and one high-confidence memory-safety regression found by fuzz harness in serving-runtime (SEC-421).
- Discussion:
  - ML runtime transitive dep (SEC-412): Jon confirmed upstream patch exists but breaks older quantization tests. Agreed to pin patched version for prod only and run extended integration tests on dedicated staging pool.
  - Monitoring agent CVE-2026-1023: low severity, but high deployment footprint. Decision: schedule rolling update next maintenance window (2026-03-10). Priya to coordinate with infra and SRE.
  - Fuzz finding (SEC-421) in serving-runtime: high confidence, reproducer attached. Liam will open hotfix branch and run CI sanitizer builds. If reproducer triggers reliably, we plan hotfix + emergency canary.
- Decisions:
  - Prioritize SEC-421 (serving-runtime) as P0 until patch validated.
  - SEC-412 handled as P2 for code compatibility; pin in prod for now.
- Action items:
  - Liam: hotfix branch for SEC-421 + sanitizer CI (due 2026-03-05).
  - Jon: prepare compatibility tests & pin plan for SEC-412 (due 2026-03-09).
  - Priya: schedule monitoring-agent update for 2026-03-10 maintenance window and update runbook (due 2026-03-08).

2) Secrets scanning (false positives + rollout)
- Context: Blockers surfaced from developers complaining about noisy alerts from the pre-commit secret scanner (many infra keys false-positive flagged in internal test accounts).
- Discussion:
  - Current scanner config is too permissive; high FP rate slowing dev workflow. Maya shared quick stats: ~120 alerts last week, ~78% false positive after manual review.
  - Proposed short-term fix: add allowlist for known test keys + disable regex for short base64-like tokens until we improve heuristics.
  - Long-term: integrate ML-based classifier and strengthen detector metadata (file context, repo owner, token TTL).
- Decisions:
  - Apply short-term allowlist + update pre-commit hook config (applies to mono-repo only) by EOD 2026-03-05.
  - Begin prototyping ML classifier; seed dataset from historical FP/TP labeled alerts.
- Action items:
  - Maya: push pre-commit config change + communicate to repo owners (done by 2026-03-05).
  - Carlos (async): export labeled alerts for ML seed dataset and drop in SEC drive (due 2026-03-07).
  - Samira: draft RFC for ML-based secret detector (first draft by 2026-03-18).

3) Threat modeling backlog prioritization
- We reviewed top 12 items in the threat model inventory (Confluence link in artifacts). Focus areas: model-supply chain, private deployment network isolation, and new third-party exporter integration.
- Discussion:
  - Model-supply chain (models fetched from external registries): need clearer attestation/metadata and optional SBOM for model artifacts. Priya proposed adding a model-ingest policy requiring checksum + provenance header.
  - Private deployments: customers asked for stronger network defaults; suggestion to provide a hardened baseline config (deny-by-default egress + mandatory KMS integration).
  - Exporter integration: medium risk; schedule as Q2 work.
- Decisions:
  - Prioritize model-supply chain protections as next sprint's design work (owner: Priya).
  - Private deployment baseline: create a baseline template and marketing one-pager for customer review (owner: Jon + Solutions Eng).
- Action items:
  - Priya: design doc for model-ingest policy + compliance checklist (draft by 2026-03-17).
  - Jon: baseline network hardening template + coordinate with Solutions Eng for customer feedback (draft by 2026-03-20).

4) Operational notes / standup snippets
- Standup highlights this week:
  - Samira: coordinating with product on rollout cadence for new secrets policy; blocked waiting on legal review for telemetry changes.
  - Jon: compatibility tests for dependency pinning in pipeline; no blockers.
  - Priya: threat model design work start; needs sandbox access (SRE ticket INFRA-389).
  - Liam: working on sanitizer CI and has a flaky test causing churn; will isolate in separate CI job.
- Blockers:
  - Legal review required for secret telemetry change (Samira) - outreach to legal sent 2026-03-03, speed request sent via Slack.
  - Sandbox access for Priya - INFRA-389 opened; SRE to expedite.

5) Misc & notes to self
- Consider adding a short section in weekly notes listing "customer-impacting vulns" for GTM and customer-success briefings.
- Follow up on metrics: reduce secret-scan FP rate to <25% in 30 days.
- Remind: update incident runbook with new canary procedure for serving-runtime hotfixes.

Next sync:
- Weekly cadence: 2026-03-11 10:00 PT
- Proposed focus: post-hotfix validation for SEC-421, secrets scanner FP reduction metrics, and Priya threat-model draft review.

Minutes prepared by: Samira Patel
